Hi Alice — attaching the first-pass diagrams and a CAIQ response summary for the network/security questions. Short notes below; document and diagram thumbnails are attached.

Attachments:
- dedicated-private-segmentation-diagram.svg (SVG, 450KB)
- caiq-responses-summary.docx (Word, 120KB)
- network-assurance-mapping-draft.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)

Executive summary: 
- Control plane is separated from data plane via dedicated management VPCs per customer for Dedicated and per-cluster control plane in Private. We call out control plane access paths and assume mutual TLS for internal RPCs.
- Tenant fencing: compute and storage namespaces are isolated at both orchestration and network layers. For Dedicated we use isolated GPU pools + VPC segmentation; Private offers optional host-level enclaves.
- KMS boundaries: customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) are supported in Private; for Dedicated we provide dedicated key rings per-tenant in the customer KMS project. Details in the CAIQ mapping doc.
- Egress: explicit egress routes with NAT gateways and egress firewall policies. We document default deny posture and per-tenant allow lists for host egress.
- Airlock option: described as an optional transit gateway plus inspection/bastion workflow; operational impact noted (latency and maintenance windows).

Open items for Veridian: 
1) Confirm whether Veridian requires HSM-backed keys for Dedicated (affects KMS mapping).
2) Any preferred IP allowlist ranges for peering/monitoring endpoints?
3) Which control-plane logs you want exported (we map available exports in the doc).

If the above looks good we can finalize the CAIQ subset and produce an annotated PNG for inclusion in your audit packet. Would you like a quick 30-min walkthrough tomorrow (June 19) at 10:00am PT?

Thanks,
